corpus.carve_bytes_source: sealed cache identity (sha256 of y and g); the cache carries no build metadata

candidates.why: 0003's incumbent verbatim (run_study.py make_model 'hgb', run_carve.py's explicit last-10% validation split); every other parameter at the sklearn 1.9.0 default
horizon only: was the incumbent stopped early by patience 10 on a 26-class validation loss that moves by thousandths? (at 2048 it fired after 22 iterations at 100000 rows and 38 at 500000)
lower rate, longer horizon: the standard boosting trade; the cap of 300 bounds the worst-case cost
capacity plus regularisation plus a lower rate together: 800000 rows x 26 classes supports bigger trees than 63 leaves, and the deep-tree baseline gained 0.1459 -> 0.1812 from depth 8 to 16 at 4096
the wide-tree end with the leaf-size regulariser that matters for 26-way splits on noisy histogram columns; run_study.py records that unregularised capacity collapsed the 100k rung once

per-split column subsampling: feature_ablation.json banks that the 555 alignment columns carry little, i.e. about half the 1108-column vector is near-redundant, and subsampling is the cheap decorrelator (new in sklearn 1.4, unavailable to the 0003 pilot)
the low-variance end: small trees with heavy L2; at chance 0.038 and top-1 0.17 the task is signal-starved and a lower-variance learner can beat a higher-capacity one at the same data

the incumbent with a CHUNK-GROUPED early-stopping split instead of the inherited fragment-level one, which shares 18614 chunks with its fitting rows at 500000 rows in 0012 (measured 2026-09-03): isolates whether the content-leaking validation split stops the incumbent at the wrong iteration
0003's logistic verbatim (LogisticRegression(max_iter=400), lbfgs, C 1.0, raw features): the frozen-set bar at 0.1392; its confirmatory reproduction within 0.005 is a validity clause
the 0003 recipe allowed to run to 1500 lbfgs iterations on raw features: tests whether the 400-iteration cap alone held the frozen bar down (0003's run hit the cap)
standardised inputs with C 1.0: the single most standard fix for an lbfgs logistic on 1108 unscaled hand-engineered columns
standardised, stronger regularisation
standardised, the strongest regularisation on the list, so the C axis is bracketed below
standardised, weak regularisation, so the C axis is bracketed above
L3 with a longer iteration budget: convergence at 1500 against 1000 on the standardised problem
L4 with a longer iteration budget; max_iter is capped at 1500 across the head so the worst-case logistic fit is bounded
0003's depth3_tree verbatim (DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3, random_state=0), gini, min_samples_leaf 1): 0.0969 banked
depth is the head's definition and is not searched; criterion x min_samples_leaf is the whole knob space at depth 3, searched so that every frozen head with a hyperparameter gets the same treatment

as D2, entropy criterion
as D2, entropy criterion

as D2, entropy criterion
0003's depth8_tree verbatim (0.1459 banked); the deep_tree head subsumes 0003's depth8_tree and depth16_tree heads and carries the floor max(0.1459, 0.1812) = 0.1812 (non-gutenberg 0.1891)
0003's depth16_tree verbatim: the binding expanded-set baseline at 0.1812 (0.1891 non-gutenberg)
depth 16 with leaf-size regularisation: the first-order fix for an unpruned depth-16 tree on 800000 rows
the next step on the axis that banked 0.0969 -> 0.1459 -> 0.1812 from depth 3 to 8 to 16
depth 24, regularised
unlimited depth, unpruned: the maximal single tree
unlimited depth, light leaf regularisation
unlimited depth with min_samples_leaf 20: plausibly the strongest single tree sklearn can build here, and the candidate most likely to RAISE the expanded bar
no hyperparameter; confirmatory fit only, as in 0003 (0.0385 banked)
no hyperparameter; confirmatory fit only (0.0387 banked)
a depth-1 tree has no meaningful knob; confirmatory fit only (0.0751 banked; non-gutenberg 0.0769)
